items.title: Javon Jackson interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 3, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: Like if you take the Joe Biden statement where he said if you’re not voting for me you ain’t black.

ctx.x: Well that’s distressing. I don’t know if you have any thoughts about how that gets changed. How do you legislate a change in attitude, or make people more aware?

Well again, almost anybody you can speak to a black person has had some kind of common occurrence like that, where you walk into an elevator and there’s a white person, a woman, older or possibly maybe elderly, who kind of clutched her bag. Or there’s always maybe a sense that you’re looked upon as a certain class per se unless in certain situations unless you maybe dress the part. I mean I’ve always kind of felt sometimes if I’m going into — I used to, not so much now but still possibly — but going into a…

to look at that and find out where we can start, day one, move it forward but also realize the history of what we’ve experienced as black people shapes those communities. So what’s wrong with taking 50 million dollars, 60 million dollars, and stacking it back into those communities. And people say oh well we can’t do reparations. Wait a minute, some of these people from the time that we’ve had Reconstruction forward have never really had a shot. So they came out of slavery and just generations and generations…
